title: Catch chip data that disagrees with the message

blocks.text: A terminal vendor shipped a firmware update, and since then the network has rejected a few of your acquirer's chip authorizations as "chip data inconsistent with the message". Before you forward a request, you want to know the same thing the network will check: does the chip data in DE 55 agree with the ISO fields it mirrors?

`ChipConsistency.mismatches` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/ChipConsistency.java` already walks the four mirrored tags and collects the ones that disagree. Finish the two methods marked `TODO`:

items: `chipDigits`: the digits a chip value holds, or `null` when DE 55 doesn't have the tag;
`agrees`: whether those digits match the field the tag mirrors, or `null` when the message doesn't carry that field.

blocks.text: The terminals sell in several currencies, refund and dispense cash as well as sell, and DE 55 holds whatever the card and the terminal put there. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: a message whose chip data agrees with its fields, and a message without chip data, report nothing
every mirrored tag that disagrees with its field is reported, in the order 9F02, 5F2A, 9C, 9A
numeric chip values are BCD and are compared as the digits their bytes hold, never as binary numbers
5F2A holds four digits, a zero and then the three digits of DE 49
9A is YYMMDD, so its month and day, not its year and month, are compared with DE 13
tags are found by parsing the TLV list, so bytes inside another value that look like a tag are ignored
a chip value whose ISO field is absent is not compared, so it is not reported

origin.section: 18.2. Chip Values Are BCD Digits, and Each Must Agree With the ISO Field It Mirrors

concepts: 9F02, 5F2A, 9C and 9A mirror DE 4, DE 49, DE 3 and DE 13; their values are BCD digits, found by parsing, compared only when both sides are present.
